title: Foundations: Disco Pop - The Complete Guide
summary: What Disco Pop is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Disco Pop songs: Disco was dance music perfected: four-on-the-floor kicks, octave basslines, string sections, and a mirror ball. Born in underground clubs, it ruled the late 1970s before the backlash — and never really died.

History: Philadelphia International and Salsoul built the sound; Saturday Night Fever (1977) made it global. Donna Summer, Chic, and the Bee Gees defined the peak; house music is disco's direct child.

How the songs work: Disco Pop favors the keys of Am, Em, Dm, Gm. Common forms include Extended 12-inch mixes for DJs; Verse-chorus with orchestral breaks. Players should master four-on-the-floor kick drum first, then octave basslines. Orchestral keys; guitarists funk-comp.
